fields.sample_size: all 16 water system management teams (WSMTs) of small-town systems serving more than 2,000 people in three Ghanaian districts (Akatsi and two others); focus groups and key-informant interviews with qualitative and quantitative data
fields.effect_estimate: Awareness and application of CWSA water-sector guidelines by WSMTs and district assemblies is limited; the National Community Water and Sanitation Strategy mechanism for capital maintenance expenditure works only where implemented; financial management of all WSMTs is weak; only the Akatsi WSMT had a capital account for future major maintenance; there is no control over disbursement of WSMT funds; main finance sources are tariffs, district assembly contributions and a few donor grants. The author concludes that community ownership and management needs professionalisation and stronger supervision and oversight by CWSA and the District Assemblies. Descriptive; no effect estimates.
fields.study_design: mixed-methods multiple-case study (focus groups and key-informant interviews with 16 management teams in three districts)
fields.section: Full text: Methods and data collection; Results (management models, financial management); Conclusions
fields.exact_location: Methods and data collection; Results (management models, financial management); Conclusions

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a multiple-case study of all 16 small-town water system management teams in three Ghanaian districts, read in full text 2026-10-04. Weak financial management and low application of sector guidelines; one team with a capital maintenance account; stronger CWSA and District Assembly oversight recommended. Descriptive.
